Relationship Description: Provides the pre-calculated royalty-receipt population used to reproduce the Tempo Client Financials experience. The source is populated after royalty calculations complete and contains rolled-up Earnings Line results at Statement Period, Song, Client, Source hierarchy, Contract, Income Type, Rate Type, and related processing dimensions.
Business Rule / Context: Client Financials does not aggregate raw Earnings Lines directly. It consumes the Tempo Earnings Line Summarization layer to provide faster operational access. The approved population is restricted to affiliate_income_ind = 'N'; including both 'Y' and 'N' doubles every numerical amount relative to the Tempo Client Financials screen.
Source / Basis: CREATE VIEW DDL and SME confirmation
Notes: Core upstream operational-summary relationship.

Relationship Description: Associates each calculated royalty receipt with the Client to whom the royalty activity is attributed, enabling Client-level review of income, withholding tax, NPS, Royalty Payable, Statement Period, Song, Source, and contractual context.
Business Rule / Context: Client Financials is presented from the Client perspective. Descriptive Client attributes come from the current Client record only (prior_version_ind = 'N'). Monetary values remain in the Client Originating Office currency; the Client relationship does not imply that values from different originating offices can be added without currency conversion.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN edw.tempo_client c
Notes: The LEFT JOIN preserves summarized receipts if descriptive Client metadata is unavailable.

Relationship Description: Identifies the Client record used within the originating-office processing context for the calculated royalty receipt. This provides the office-specific Client identity associated with royalty administration and reporting.
Business Rule / Context: The Originating Office Client can differ from the general Client or Primary Client identifiers exposed by the view. The current Client version is selected (prior_version_ind = 'N'). Users should retain the distinct Client roles when analyzing inter-office royalty processing or reconciling Client structures.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN edw.tempo_client c1
Notes: Client role is explicitly distinguished from client_id and primary_client_id.

Relationship Description: Associates a calculated royalty receipt with its Primary Client rollup, supporting analysis where multiple related Client records are managed or reported under a principal Client relationship.
Business Rule / Context: Primary Client is a reporting and administration context and should not automatically replace the Client or Originating Office Client in calculations. The view uses the current Primary Client version. Users should choose the Client role that matches the business question and avoid assuming the three Client identifiers are interchangeable.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN edw.tempo_client pc
Notes: Current version filter applied.

Relationship Description: Associates each calculated royalty receipt with the Client Originating Office and supplies the office name and currency used to present the financial measures.
Business Rule / Context: The Client Originating Office determines the currency context for all monetary amounts in Client Financials. Users must include currency_cd in aggregations and must not sum across originating-office currencies without an approved conversion method. The office is a reporting perspective, not necessarily the affiliate that originally collected the royalty.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN edw.tempo_orig_office oo
Notes: Critical currency relationship.

Relationship Description: Associates each calculated royalty receipt with the Contract under which the Client royalty entitlement is administered, enabling financial review within the contractual framework governing the royalty relationship.
Business Rule / Context: Contract is office-scoped and is therefore joined using both Originating Office ID and Contract ID. Only the current Contract version (prior_version_ind = 'N') is used. Contract-level analysis supports royalty servicing and deal review, but receipts may remain in the view when descriptive Contract metadata is unavailable because the relationship is a LEFT JOIN.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN edw.tempo_contract con
Notes: Composite office-and-contract join.

Relationship Description: Associates a calculated royalty receipt with the most relevant Subcontract description, adding the detailed contractual component under which the Song-level royalty was calculated.
Business Rule / Context: Tempo can contain more than one current-version row for a Subcontract ID. The view resolves this by selecting the most recently updated current record using ROW_NUMBER ordered by update_dt descending. This is a deterministic display rule and does not redefine the underlying Subcontract business key.
Source / Basis: Ranked LEFT JOIN to edw.tempo_subcontract
Notes: Latest updated current row selected.

Relationship Description: Associates each calculated Client royalty receipt with the specific Song and Song sequence that generated the royalty, enabling Song-level analysis of statement-period income, tax, NPS, payable, Source, and rate outcomes.
Business Rule / Context: Song-level royalties are part of the validated business grain. The relationship uses Song ID plus Song Sequence ID and selects the current Song version (prior_version_ind = 'N') to display the latest approved title. Aggregating above Song level can combine receipts that differ by Contract, Source, Income Type, Rate Type, or other dimensions.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN edw.tempo_song sg
Notes: Song title is descriptive enrichment.

Relationship Description: Enriches each calculated royalty receipt with the maximum Source hierarchy detail available in Tempo: Source, Sub Source, Sub Sub Source, and Original Sub Sub Source. This supports investigation of the societies, affiliates, licensees, broadcasters, digital services, and other providers associated with the royalty.
Business Rule / Context: The four Source roles are preserved separately and should not be treated as interchangeable. Lower hierarchy levels may be null where Tempo has no additional detail. Client Financials does not apply the affiliate source-hierarchy normalization used by some other SA-010 views; it exposes the identifiers stored in the underlying Client Financials summary population.
Source / Basis: Four LEFT JOINs to edw.tempo_source
Notes: Maximum available hierarchy detail is part of the grain.

Relationship Description: Associates each Source hierarchy member with one representative active country, providing geographic context for Source, Sub Source, Sub Sub Source, and Original Sub Sub Source analysis.
Business Rule / Context: For each Source ID, the view selects a single active Source Country. A record flagged primary is preferred; otherwise the most recently updated active country is selected. The rule is applied independently to all four Source roles. Source Country is descriptive context and must not automatically be interpreted as the Client country, usage territory, tax jurisdiction, or payment currency.
Source / Basis: Four ranked LEFT JOINs to edw.tempo_source_country
Notes: Primary-first, then latest-active selection.

Relationship Description: Classifies each calculated royalty receipt by its detailed Income Type and governed Income Type Group, enabling analysis of the nature of royalty income and its broader income category.
Business Rule / Context: Income Type is the more detailed classification and also supplies the Streaming Indicator. Income Type Group provides a governed lower-level grouping. Users should retain Income Type when detailed treatment matters and should not infer Streaming solely from the group name; streaming_ind is the authoritative flag exposed by the view.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN tempo_income_type; LEFT JOIN tempo_income_type_group
Notes: Reference enrichment can be absent without suppressing the receipt.

Relationship Description: Associates each calculated royalty receipt with the governed Rate Type describing the royalty calculation basis applied to the receipt.
Business Rule / Context: Allowed values are At Source (1), Receipt (2), Limited Receipt (3), and Participant (4). Rate Type provides essential calculation context and should be retained when comparing royalty outcomes. Participant treatment is especially relevant to related earnings reporting because GL Posting Amount is expected to be zero for Participant Rate Type.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN edw.tempo_rate_type rt
Notes: Governed reference domain.

Relationship Description: Associates each calculated royalty receipt with the type of royalty-processing transaction that produced or classified the financial activity.
Business Rule / Context: Transaction Type supplies processing context and can distinguish receipts with different business treatments even when Client, Song, Statement Period, and Source are the same. It is part of the technical grouping grain and should be retained in detailed reconciliation or calculation investigations.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN edw.tempo_transaction_type tt
Notes: Governed transaction reference.

Relationship Description: Associates each calculated royalty receipt with the Tempo Company and Company Group responsible for the relevant processing or ownership context.
Business Rule / Context: Company and Company Group provide organizational context for royalty receipts and may be used to explain differences in processing treatment or reporting populations. The view also separately exposes the Originating Office Company, so users should preserve the distinction between the receipt Company and the originating-office Company.
Source / Basis: LEFT JOIN tempo_company; LEFT JOIN tempo_company_group
Notes: Company roles are not interchangeable.

Relationship Description: Client Financials is the reporting-layer representation of the calculated royalty receipts and financial amounts displayed in the Tempo Client module Financial tab.
Business Rule / Context: For equivalent Client, Statement Period, Song, Source hierarchy, Contract, Income Type, Rate Type, Transaction Type, and currency selections, the view is expected to reproduce the Tempo UI amounts. Reconciliation requires affiliate_income_ind = 'N'. Differences should be investigated for filter alignment, summarization-process completion, Client Originating Office currency, and differences in displayed detail.
Source / Basis: SME-confirmed business purpose and reconciliation behavior
Notes: Logical downstream relationship rather than a physical database join.

Relationship Description: A Song may be associated with multiple active Song-Client-Contract relationships used for royalty allocation and rights administration.
Business Rule / Context: A single Song may have multiple active Contract and Client associations. Additional rows can occur when different Clients participate in the same Contract or when multiple Contracts are associated with the Song. Reports using this relationship should evaluate reporting grain prior to combining ownership-share data to prevent duplicate representation of ownership interests.
Source / Basis: SME Validation + Reporting Use Cases
Notes: This object is commonly used to identify Contract and Client participation for a Song rather than ownership percentage calculations.

Relationship Description: A Contract may be represented by multiple active Client relationships.
Business Rule / Context: Multiple Clients may participate in the same Contract and therefore appear as separate rows within tempo_active_song_rate_client_v. Direct joins between Contract/Client relationship data and ownership-share objects may create many-to-many results unless the reporting grain is reconciled before joining.
Source / Basis: SME Validation + Reporting Use Cases
Notes: Common source of row multiplication when ownership-share reporting is performed at Song or Territory level.

Relationship Description: Ownership-share records may relate to multiple active Client relationships for the same Song and Contract.
Business Rule / Context: song_share_summary_mv is maintained at Song, Territory, Writer, and Associated Contract grain, while tempo_active_song_rate_client_v is maintained at Song, Client, and Contract grain. Direct joins between these objects can multiply ownership-share rows when multiple Clients exist for the same Contract. Client or ownership information should be aggregated to a compatible reporting grain before joining.
Source / Basis: SME Validation + Reporting Use Cases
Notes: Critical relationship for ownership, repertoire, territorial share, and contract reporting. Failure to reconcile grain may overstate publisher mechanical, performance, and synchronization percentages.

Relationship Description: Associates each intercompany rate with the office whose currency is converted to USD.
Business Rule / Context: One office may have many rates over time; office lookup supplies currency_cd.
Source / Basis: Supplied DDL + SME confirmation

Relationship Description: Publishes the quarter-end Tempo rate position.
Business Rule / Context: Consumers select by Statement Period and office; DISTINCT suppresses exact duplicates.
Source / Basis: Supplied DDL + SME confirmation

Relationship Description: Associates each monthly rate with the local currency translated to USD.
Business Rule / Context: One approved rate is expected per currency and month-end period.
Source / Basis: Supplied DDL + SME confirmation

Relationship Description: Exposes Treasury-provided closing rates and audit metadata.
Business Rule / Context: Direct projection; source uniqueness and quality flow directly to the view.
Source / Basis: Supplied DDL + SME confirmation

Relationship Description: Associates each Deal-level capitalized trial-balance position with the Treasury-provided monthly closing FX rate required to translate the Client Originating Office currency into USD for Finance management reporting and month-end close.
Business Rule / Context: Join on currency_cd and the corresponding reporting month. Multiply capitalized_closing_balance_am by exchange_rate_pc to convert the local-currency balance to USD. The FX rate is a local-currency-to-USD factor and must not be inverted. The converted balance remains at P&L Client and Capitalized Accounting Period grain.
Source / Basis: Enterprise Metadata Workbook; supplied view DDL; validated US Deal Office capitalized-balance reporting use case
Notes: Use tempo_monthly_exchange_rate_v for Finance management reporting and month-end close. Do not substitute tempo_ig_fx_rates, which is governed for the Tempo Intercompany Royalty Process. Apply USD materiality thresholds after conversion. If the dates represent different days within the same reporting month, match at month level rather than requiring the date values to be identical.
